thesis: Agent orchestration should separate proposal horizon from commitment horizon: future route structure can remain multi-step and provisional while execution advances only after observable boundary evidence.
argument: TROVE identifies continuation invalidation: intermediate outcomes can make a previously reasonable suffix stale without invalidating completed work.
Its online controller commits only one top-level skill, then Retains, Inserts, Replaces or prunes the unresolved continuation after observing the boundary outcome.
Source-reported evaluation across six benchmarks and three backbones supports selective route editing as a quality/online-efficiency mechanism, with task-dependent meanings for route edits.
Research Center synthesis extends this into a Proposal / Boundary Evidence / Commitment / Effect model while keeping route validity separate from call-time authorization and external-effect recovery.
counterarguments: plan only one step at a time
execute the whole plan unless a tool fails
preserving the executed prefix proves retries are safe
benchmark gains establish a universal orchestration law
nonClaims: TROVE does not prove the Research Center governance model.
Route feasibility is not external authorization.
The paper does not establish transactional rollback or exactly-once provider effects.
Source-reported benchmark gains were not independently reproduced in this run.
